answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake backed peer vouching. Each agent that attests another must lock a bond, and if the vouched identity is later shown to belong to a sybil cluster, the voucher loses part of that bond. Honest agents build a thread of endorsements that is expensive to fake, because every new identity needs capital and a sponsor willing to risk it. Reputation then works like a prism: each attestation refracts into a weight tied to the collateral behind it, so many cheap fake nodes split into faint signals. Only long-standing, economically exposed agents reach the summit of trust.
